caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 35 of 1998
lawyer:
Md Shahidul Alam Chowdhury, Advocate, instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate on-Record ----- For the Petitioner.
Amirul Islam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent No.1.
Not represented - Respondent Nos. 2-5
parties:
Government of the people's Republic of Bangladesh ------ Petitioner. 
Vs
East West Property Development Private Ltd & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal CJ: This petition for leave to appeal by respondent  No. 1 petitioner is from the judgment and order dated 14-08-97 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3165 of 1997 making the Rule Nisi absolute. 

 2. The writ-petitioner-respondent claims to have purchased 47.75 acres of land which originally belonged to Bhawal Raj Estate and which was taken over by the Court of Wards under the Court of Wards Act, 1879. The Bhawal Raj Estate instituted a suit in 1938 against the Government respondents and in 1939 the suit was disposed of by a compromise decree in between the parties. Thereafter, the properties of Bhawal Raj Estate were sold to different persons including the predecessors-in-interest of the writ-petitioner-respondent. The SA record was finally published in the names of the predecessors-in-interest of the writ-petitioner-respondent in 1963. Since 1939 the said predecessors were possessing their purchased portion of the suit properties as owners and paying rent to the Government. In 1987 the writ-petitioner-respondent purchased 47.75 acres of land from the various S.A recorded owners and had established a Housing Estate known as Bashundhara which is in a development stage. 

 3. The present petitioner and other respondent in the writ petition instituted a suit in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka namely, Title Suit No.11 of 1997 on 19-1-97 for a decree for declaration of title to a part of the suit land, namely, 1.24 acre as a test case. Thereafter respondent No. 3, Manager, Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate, Land Reforms Board issued a notice dated 19-5-97 and later the notice was issued as a public notice in the newspapers on 24-5-97 directing the writ petitioner-respondent to vacate the suit properties measuring 47.75 acres. 

 5. The petitioner as respondent contended in its affidavit-in-opposition that since no permission was taken from the Court of Wards the successive transfer of the suit property ultimately to the writ petitioner was illegal. 

 6. The High Court Division found that the writ-petitioner annexed many papers and documents of title and possession to show that since 1939 and again from 1963 different owners of this vast property have been possessing their respective portions by mutating their names and paying rents to the Government. Since 1939 the respondent-petitioner and the other respondents did not challenge the right and title of the predecessors in interest of the writ-petitioner. Therefore, their claim of little at such a belated stage after about 58 years cannot be entertained in the eye of law. Besides, during the pendency of the writ petition respondent No.1 petitioner filed an application for injunction in Title Suit No.l1 of 1997. The petitioner's prayer for temporary injunction was rejected by the trial Court by judgment and order dated 23-6-97. The issuance of the impugned notice of eviction was illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 7. Md Shahidul Alam Chowdhury, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the Court of Wards, acting under the Court of Wards Act, 1879 does not perform a function in connection with the affairs of the republic but in connection with the affairs of private property. Therefore, the impugned notice could only be challenged in a civil Court but not in the writ jurisdiction. 

 10. Mr Chowdhury's next contention is that the High Court Division having held that the petitioner's claim of title at the belated stage after about 58 years cannot be entertained in the eye of law is an observation beyond jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. These observations will prejudice the case of respondent No.1 in Title Suit No. 11 of 1997 and will also prejudice the petitioner's claim of title to the remaining lands covered by 47.75 acres. 

 11. Mr Amirul Islam readily concedes that since the dispute is of a civil nature the writ petitioner will be contented if the impugned notices are declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect and as for the suit property and to the remaining land of 47.75 acres, the writ petitioner will also remain contented at fighting the issue before the civil Court, if necessary. 

 12. In view of the above we think that it was absolutely necessary for the High Court Division to comment on the petitioner's title to and possession of 1.24 acre of land and generally on 47.75 acres of land in a manner favourable to the writ petitioner. Those findings of the High Court Division will be taken into account as a finding of fact or law either by the trial Court in Title Suit No. 11 of 1997 or by any other Court in any future litigation regarding the title to 47.75 acres of land.
